standard_prerequisites.name: The circle as a higher inductive type
standard_prerequisites.statement: The circle has a point constructor and a loop constructor, so a map out of it into any type with a point x and a loop p at x is given by those two data.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what turns a hypothetical triviality of the loop into an equation in an arbitrary type.

standard_prerequisites.name: The universe is not a set
standard_prerequisites.statement: Not every type is a set: the universe contains a type whose loop space has two distinct elements.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the contradiction the proof arrives at, and it is retained as a navigation pointer.

core_obligations: Assume that the generating loop equals reflexivity at the base point (source line 448).

Use the recursion principle of the circle to build, for an arbitrary type A with a point x and a loop p at x, a map from the circle sending base to x and the generating loop to p (source lines 449-450).
Evaluate that map on the assumed equality to conclude p equals reflexivity for every such p (source lines 450-451).
Conclude that every loop of every type is trivial, hence that every type is a set, contradicting the known counterexample in the universe (source lines 451-452).

proof_roadmap.step: Assume the loop is trivial and build the family of maps out of the circle.
Derive the triviality of all loops and contradict the universe not being a set.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 444-446 (book Theorem 6.4.1): the generating loop of the circle is not equal to the reflexivity path at its base point. The statement is a single disequality and the proof (source lines 447-452) has to manufacture the contradiction: it assumes the equality, then uses the recursion principle of the circle to transport that assumption to an arbitrary type carrying an arbitrary loop, concluding that every loop of every type is trivial and therefore that every type is a set, which contradicts the universe not being one. The step from a triviality of one loop to a global triviality of loops is the substance, and the statement contains none of it.
